summary: Hansa Teutonica is a lean, brutal network-building game where you extend trade routes by placing merchants, but rival players can bump you off contested routes, forcing tense calculations about when to lock in a route versus upgrade your abilities. The tech-track upgrades (more actions, swapping pieces, moving through occupied spaces) create a snowballing efficiency race that rewards tight optimization over any theme.
praised: tight, efficient action-point puzzle with almost no downtime
upgrade tracks give satisfying engine-building progression
high replayability across different maps/expansions in the Big Box
criticised: thin theme, essentially an abstract optimization game
can feel mean when your routes get bumped repeatedly
analysis paralysis for new players facing many viable strategies
map/route knowledge advantage for experienced players

interaction.kind: displacement and area majority contention over shared routes

scoring.why: points come from completed routes, upgraded abilities, and end-game bonuses, but efficient network control dominates
